visuals.title: What refeeding hits
visuals.text: Arrhythmia and heart failure (wet beriberi); confusion, seizures, Wernicke's encephalopathy; electrolyte collapse.

glossary.morbidity: Illness or harm caused by a disease.
glossary.functional decline: Losing the ability to do everyday tasks such as walking, washing or dressing.
glossary.eating disorders: Mental illnesses with abnormal eating, such as anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa.
glossary.frailty: Reduced physical reserve in older people, so minor illness causes a big decline.
glossary.dementia: Progressive decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life.
glossary.alcohol misuse: Drinking at a level that harms health; also causes poor diet and vitamin loss.
glossary.hair thinning: Loss of hair density, a sign of protein and micronutrient deficiency.
glossary.reduced exercise tolerance: Becoming tired or breathless with less activity than before.
glossary.peripheral oedema: Swelling of the legs or other dependent parts from fluid in the tissues.
glossary.micronutrient: A vitamin or mineral needed in small amounts, such as iron, zinc or B12.
glossary.electrolyte: A charged mineral in blood, such as sodium, potassium, phosphate or magnesium.
glossary.poor wound healing: Slow repair of skin and tissue injury, often from protein and vitamin deficiency.
glossary.cirrhosis: Permanent scarring of the liver that impairs its function.
glossary.B12: Vitamin B12, needed for red cells and nerves; deficiency causes anaemia and neuropathy.
glossary.IgG: Immunoglobulin G, the main antibody class in blood.
glossary.bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
glossary.foul-smelling stool: Offensive stool, often pale and greasy when fat is not absorbed.
glossary.vitamin A: A fat-soluble vitamin needed for vision in dim light and healthy skin.
glossary.dressings: Coverings applied to wounds or sores to protect them and help healing.
glossary.supportive mattress: A pressure-relieving mattress that spreads weight to prevent and treat pressure sores.
glossary.4 Ds: Diarrhoea, dermatitis, dementia and death: the features of pellagra.
glossary.dermatitis: Inflammation of the skin; in pellagra a rash on sun-exposed areas.
glossary.insulin surge: A sharp rise in insulin when carbohydrate is eaten after starvation.
glossary.seizures: Episodes of abnormal electrical brain activity causing fits or altered awareness.
glossary.heart failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.nutritional assessment: Full review of diet, weight, body build, bloods and needs by a clinician or dietitian.
glossary.unplanned weight loss: Weight lost without trying, a key warning sign of illness or malnutrition.
glossary.acute disease effect: MUST item scoring patients so unwell they are likely to have no intake for over 5 days.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: sodium, potassium, urea and creatinine, a test of kidney function.
glossary.LFTs: Liver function tests, including albumin, bilirubin and liver enzymes.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.inflammation: The body's response to injury or infection, which lowers albumin production.
glossary.dietician: A health professional who assesses diet and plans nutrition support (also spelt dietitian).
glossary.high-calorie/high-protein diet: Food choices that pack more energy and protein into each portion.
glossary.underlying cause: The disease driving the malnutrition, such as cancer or malabsorption.
glossary.small bowel mucosa: The inner lining of the small intestine, where most nutrients are absorbed.
glossary.bile salts: Detergent-like molecules from bile that break fat into small droplets for absorption.
glossary.fat metabolism: Burning stored fat for energy, as the body does during starvation.
glossary.cofactor: A helper molecule an enzyme needs to work; thiamine is one for carbohydrate metabolism.
glossary.carbohydrate metabolism: The chemical breakdown of sugars and starch to release energy.
glossary.NADP: A niacin-derived molecule used in building and repair reactions in cells.
glossary.rapidly dividing tissues: Tissues that renew quickly, like skin and gut lining, so suffer first in deficiency.
glossary.CNS: Central nervous system: the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.NICE CG32: NICE guideline on nutrition support for adults: screening, oral, enteral and parenteral feeding.
